scope: Targeted narrative review of primary advisories, maintainer accounts, discoverer methods and dated telemetry. Not an exhaustive systematic review or an independent vulnerability reproduction.
search_examples: Node.js AI discovered security vulnerability October 2026 high severity
selection: Prefer stable maintainer/CVE identifiers and directly observed methods. Retain contrary and time-limited findings. Do not count syndication, branding aliases or downstream advisories as independent discoveries. Exclude unrelated incidents lacking established AI involvement from claims of AI-discovered vulnerabilities.

w3techs_snapshot.denominator: websites whose server-side programming language is known

censys_snapshot.unit_definition: IP address or hostname plus port; not unique websites, machines or organizations
limitations: vendor backports can preserve old version labels
unknown versions excluded from affected/fixed classification

cisa_snapshot.retrieval_method: direct HTTPS request to official public JSON feed, parsed by exact CVE ID

patch_milestones.policy: Historical milestones, not a substitute for current maintainer/vendor advice. PHP's 23 October separate session notice and 26 October dependency rebuild mean a single source-runtime version is not a universal all-issues-safe assertion.

release_recheck: Refresh catalog entries, primary advisories, patches and browser-selected dashboards at November publication and monthly thereafter. Append new observations; do not silently replace the dated intake snapshot or present it as a current release receipt.
